issues.claim: implications_for_consultancy[0]: the accepted band is "roughly $250-$500/month" because "four independent national vendors price their entry human plans into that window - Ruby $250/$395, Abby Starter/Essential $164/$329, AnswerConnect $350/$395 and PATLive $189-$479"
issues.problem: Four of the ten prices cited to justify the window fall below its $250 lower bound (Abby $164, PATLive $189; PATLive $479 is inside), so the sourced prices support a band of about $164-$500, not $250-$500. The stated window contradicts the brief's own figures even though it is labeled inference.
issues.fix: Either widen the band to roughly $165-$500 (and keep the "pilot at $300-$500 reads as normal" conclusion, which still holds), or rephrase to "entry human plans cluster at roughly $165-$500, with national brands at $250-$395".

issues.claim: implications_for_consultancy[4]: "those tiers are message-only or AI-with-backup, they exclude transfers, intake and integrations" (about the $15-$55 self-serve tiers)
issues.problem: Contradicted by the brief's own sourced data: AnsweringService.com's "Answer" tier at $40/month on the same cited page includes warm call transfers and unlimited contacts, so "they exclude transfers" is false for the $40 tier (CRM/web-form entry and appointment setting are indeed confined to the $55 MyAssistant tier).
issues.fix: Narrow the claim: "the $15 and $25 tiers are message-only; transfers start at $40, and lead entry into CRMs/appointment setting only appear at $55" — the conclusion (do not compete there) survives unchanged.

issues.claim: what_is_included_vs_extra: "AnswerConnect bills whole minutes rounded up ... hold, transfer/patch time and after-call work count toward billed time (rounding per vendor page, included-activity detail per third-party tracker)" — source_url given as https://www.answerconnect.com/plans-direct
issues.problem: The vendor page confirms only the full-minute rounding and the first-30-short-interactions exemption. The hold/transfer/after-call-work billing detail is not on that page; the brief itself says it comes from a third-party tracker, but no URL for that tracker is given, so the most consequential part of the claim (what counts as billable time) is not traceable from the source_url supplied.
issues.fix: Add the tracker URL (https://www.answeringprices.com/answerconnect/pricing/, which states hold, transfers/patches and after-call work are billed, citing answerconnect.com/termsofservice and the vendor billing guide) alongside the vendor page, or cite AnswerConnect's own terms/help-centre page directly.

issues.claim: caveats[0]: "a third-party tracker notes Ruby raised prices in December 2024 and again in December 2025"
issues.problem: No source_url or tracker name is given for this repricing claim, and I did not verify it on any page; it is presented in the caveat list without attribution.
issues.fix: Name and link the tracker, or soften to "Ruby's page assets are dated December 2025, which suggests a recent repricing that I did not confirm".

issues.claim: implications_for_consultancy[2]: a $150-$400/month managed fee sits "on top of whatever platform plan the client buys" and does "not push the client past what they currently pay" (citing buyer-reported $450-$900/month)
issues.problem: Arithmetic tension rather than a price error: a $350-$500 platform plan plus a $150-$400 fee lands at roughly $500-$900, i.e. at or above the top of the cited buyer-reported range and above the $225-$450 reports. As worded the sentence overstates the headroom.
issues.fix: Say the fee keeps a mid-tier client at roughly $500-$800/month, near the upper end of reported spend, rather than "without pushing past" it.
